symbols.name: input length
symbols.meaning: The number of bits in each of the two input integers.
symbols.quote: Let $n$ be the number of bits in each of the two input integers.

symbols.name: exponent gap
symbols.meaning: The fixed positive constant 2^{-182} by which the exponent of the logarithmic factor falls below one.

symbols.name: machine A
symbols.meaning: The single fixed deterministic Turing machine that multiplies the inputs in the theorem.
symbols.quote: Call this machine $A$, and let $T_A(n)$ be its worst-case number of steps on inputs of length $n$.

symbols.name: running time
symbols.meaning: The worst-case number of steps machine A takes on inputs of length n.
symbols.quote: Call this machine $A$, and let $T_A(n)$ be its worst-case number of steps on inputs of length $n$.

symbols.name: first input
symbols.meaning: The first of the two binary input strings, each of length n.
symbols.quote: The inputs are $x$ and $y$, two binary strings of length $n$, written as $x\#y$.

symbols.name: second input
symbols.meaning: The second of the two binary input strings, each of length n.
symbols.quote: The inputs are $x$ and $y$, two binary strings of length $n$, written as $x\#y$.

symbols.name: binary value
symbols.meaning: The function giving the nonnegative integer value of a binary string, with its leftmost bit most significant.
symbols.quote: For a binary string $x$, $\mathrm{val}(x)$ denotes its nonnegative integer value, with the leftmost bit most significant.

symbols.name: base-two logarithm
symbols.meaning: The base-two logarithm of n, rounded up to an integer and at least 1.
symbols.quote: Write $\lg n = \max\{\lceil \log_2 n\rceil, 1\}$ for the base-two logarithm of $n$, rounded up and at least 1.

relations.quote: It refutes the [n log n optimality conjecture](n-log-n-conjecture.md) in this model.
The theorem is stated for the [fixed-tape machine model](fixed-tape-model.md): one machine with a fixed finite alphabet and a fixed finite number of tapes.
The first step reduces multiplication to a [radix-digit convolution](radix-digit-convolution.md) of short integer coefficients, obtained by splitting each input into radix digits.
The radix-digit coefficients are placed on distinct prime cyclic axes by a [Chinese-remainder map](chinese-remainder-map.md) that preserves convolution.
The power saving comes from the [rank-saving recursion](rank-saving-recursion.md), in which each call splits into smaller calls on streams of a fraction of the volume.
The transforms are laid out by a [transform layout](transform-layout.md) that places the selected bits of all axes at a common offset, so that the butterfly layer applies to each transform round.
The method keeps the source and target coordinate permutations inside the [transform identity with retained permutations](transform-identity.md), so they need not be executed as sorts.
It uses [prime source lengths](prime-source-lengths.md): distinct odd primes chosen close to the powers of two.

relations.predicate: converts the last cyclic coordinate by
relations.quote: The last cyclic coordinate is converted by a [phase twist](phase-twist.md) into a coordinate of a polynomial ring.

The remaining axes are handled by [convolution over the polynomial ring](polynomial-ring-convolution.md), which computes the convolution with two forward synthetic transforms, a pointwise product and an opposite transform.
The machine adds the selected bits of the address chunks by [packed selected-bit addition](packed-bit-addition.md), which uses cyclic shifts of whole chunks and a deterministic correction.
The algorithm recovers the coefficients by rounding, which is justified by [exact coefficient recovery](recovery-and-error.md): the error is below one half.
[Carry propagation](carry-propagation.md) turns the recovered coefficients into the exact binary product.
